correctness.rationale: For two hits at a<b with exponent difference t, the identity h d=2^u(2^t-1) and n>=0 give exactly the odd-divisibility and inequality conditions; all such progressions give the same word after power-of-two normalization. Conversely the frozen n,d are integral and attain the word, allowing n=0. For three hits the odd first Mersenne factor is coprime to 2^t, forcing 2^t to divide the spacing after b. Above the cutoff t=floor(log_2 k), this excludes a third hit and the start constraint forces a=0. Each exceptional pair {0,b} is realizable by an arbitrarily large t divisible by the order of 2 modulo odd(b) (with modulus 1 separate). The printed divisibility argument is read precisely as: q/gcd(q,2^s-1) divides b for an intermediate exponent s; that actual divisor is at least (2^t-1)/(2^(t/2)-1)>b, not that the lower bound itself divides b. This establishes the claimed contradiction without changing the theorem or construction. Zero and singleton words come from unbounded gaps. The divisor estimates for a=0 and a>=1 each cost at most 4k/(1-1/sqrt(2)); first three families contribute precisely 2k distinct words, including the k=1 case. In the first estimate, 1+log_2 k<=2sqrt(k) follows by applying the tangent bound for log to sqrt(k) at 2. The all-length proof is analytic; the uploaded finite checker was inspected, not executed, and is not used as exhaustion.

evidence: Konieczny–Müllner give r^k exp(o(k)) for effective alphabet size r; here the leading digit automaton has a synchronizing dead-zero output via 11, so effective r=1. The structural low-complexity result inspected has a uniform-recurrence scope.

value.rationale: Powers of two form a canonical sparse automatic support. The finite generator replaces an unbounded progression search with explicit bounded parameters, handles arbitrary factor length and can certify attainable masks and exact counts at a chosen length. Linear growth is a significant refinement of the general subexponential or specific quadratic estimates and follows from structural constraints on several hits, not from a table of small instances.
